title: 15s cross-device refetch can silently discard an edit that hasn't finished its 500ms debounce/network round-trip
where: index.html:2547-2574 (poll/refetch effect), specifically the guard at 2557 and the applyData call at 2561; interacts with the debounced save at 2453-2487 (500ms timer at 2485)
detail: The comment at index.html:2540-2543 claims the poll is 'guarded by updated_at AND content-equality so we never ... clobber unsaved local edits.' In fact `normalize()` (2550) only prevents re-applying byte-identical content (guards against echoing an already-synced row). It has no way to detect 'this device has a local edit that is still sitting in its 500ms debounce timer, or whose saveToSupabase call is still in flight, and hasn't reached the cloud yet.' `refetch()` only checks `hydratedForUser.current===user.id` (2553) before calling `applyData(row.data,{keepPeriod:true})` (2561) whenever `row.updatedAt` is newer than `lastSeenAt.current` and the fetched content differs from the current in-memory serialization — which it necessarily will differ whenever there is a pending, not-yet-saved local edit, since that edit by definition isn't reflected in either the fetched row or (yet) anywhere durable.
failure: Same account signed in on two devices/tabs, A and B, both hydrated and in sync (lastSeenAt equal). Device A edits something (e.g. adds a shift) and its save completes, advancing the cloud row's updated_at. Moments later Device B makes an unrelated edit (e.g. corrects the base rate) — B's own 500ms debounce timer starts, and the network round-trip to Supabase hasn't completed yet. If B's `setInterval(refetch,15000)` tick, or a `focus`/`visibilitychange` event (2568-2571), fires during that window, `refetch()` sees A's newer `updated_at`, sees the fetched content differs from B's current state (because it doesn't yet include B's edit, which never reached the cloud), and calls `applyData(row.data,{keepPeriod:true})` — replacing ALL of B's in-memory state, including the edit just made, with A's snapshot. There is no merge, no conflict warning, and no backup: `writeBackup` (2273-2274) is invoked only when a cloud save FAILS, never when a remote refetch overwrites in-memory state. B's edit is gone with no indication anything happened, and B's own still-pending debounced save (now reflecting the reverted state) will shortly re-persist that reverted state to the cloud.
fix: Before applying a remote row in `refetch()`, check whether a local save is currently pending or in flight (e.g. track a `saveInFlight`/`pendingLocalEdit` ref set when the debounce timer is armed or `saveToSupabase` is awaited, cleared once the write lands) and skip/defer the apply — or queue the refetched row and re-check content-equality once the pending local save resolves — instead of unconditionally overwriting state whenever content differs from the last-seen snapshot.
